title: Selling "Blues in My Heart" to Irving Mills
summary: He sold his first published tune to Mills for $25 and later renewed the copyright with royalties.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Were you at that time -- do you remember being with Chick Webb at that time?
No. At that time, I was with Fletcher Henderson. We were playing at Connie's Carney's Inn.
Right. And was that written, in a sense, for the Henderson band?
I just wrote it ... just a song I wrote, you know?
Do you remember how it became published? I mean, what were the circumstances of its publication?

I think what happened, I believe I either took it to Irving Mills or I probably made an arrangement for the band and Irving came in the club and heard us play it one night. And showed interest in it, and I gave it to him for his publishing company -- as a matter of fact, I suppose I should say I sold it to him for $25, because that is what I received for it.

And for 28 years I received no further compensation for it -- no royalties, but when the time came around to renew the copyright, I gave it to the same publishing company -- Mills again -- and but this time with a royalty agreement.
Yes, an inflationary increase -- but with no bonus for all the years that they had it for nothing.
This was your first published tune.
And I believe your first recorded tune. Is that also true?
